sanskrit: gāndhāry uvāca aiśvaryakāma duṣṭātman vṛddhānāṃ śāsanātiga aiśvaryajīvite hitvā pitaraṃ māṃ ca bāliśa
english: Gāndhārī said: O you who crave dominion, O wicked-souled one, O transgressor of the elders' commands — foolish one, having abandoned your father and me for the sake of a life built on power,

sanskrit: vardhayan durhṛdāṃ prītiṃ māṃ ca śokena vardhayan nihato bhīmasenena smartāsi vacanaṃ pituḥ
english: increasing the joy of the ill-willed and multiplying my grief — slain by Bhīmasena, you will then remember your father's words.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca dayito 'si rājan kṛṣṇasya dhṛtarāṣṭra nibodha me yasya te saṃjayo dūto yas tvāṃ śreyasi yokṣyate
english: Vyāsa said: You are dear to Kṛṣṇa, O king Dhṛtarāṣṭra — hear me. Sañjaya, whose envoy he is, will engage you in what is beneficial.

sanskrit: jānāty eṣa hṛṣīkeśaṃ purāṇaṃ yac ca vai navam śuśrūṣamāṇam ekāgraṃ mokṣyate mahato bhayāt
english: This one knows Hṛṣīkeśa in both his ancient and his present aspect; by listening to him with single-pointed devotion, one is freed from a great fear.

sanskrit: vaicitravīrya puruṣāḥ krodhaharṣatamovṛtāḥ sitā bahuvidhaiḥ pāśair ye na tuṣṭāḥ svakair dhanaiḥ
english: O son of Vicitravīrya, men enveloped by anger, elation, and delusion, bound by snares of many kinds, who are not content with their own wealth —

sanskrit: yamasya vaśam āyānti kāmamūḍhāḥ punaḥ punaḥ andhanetrā yathaivāndhā nīyamānāḥ svakarmabhiḥ
english: those blinded by desire come again and again under the sway of Yama, led by their own deeds like the blind leading the blind.

sanskrit: eṣa ekāyanaḥ panthā yena yānti manīṣiṇaḥ taṃ dṛṣṭvā mṛtyum atyeti mahāṃs tatra na sajjate
english: This is the one path by which the wise travel; having seen it, the great soul transcends death and is not ensnared there.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca aṅga saṃjaya me śaṃsa panthānam akutobhayam yena gatvā hṛṣīkeśaṃ prāpnuyāṃ śāntim uttamām
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Come, Sañjaya, tell me the path free from all fear, by treading which I may reach Hṛṣīkeśa and attain the highest peace.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca nākṛtātmā kṛtātmānaṃ jātu vidyāj janārdanam ātmanas tu kriyopāyo nānyatrendriyanigrahāt
english: Sañjaya said: One who has not disciplined the self can never know Janārdana, who has disciplined his self. Yet the means for the self lies nowhere else but in the restraint of the senses.

sanskrit: indriyāṇām udīrṇānāṃ kāmatyāgo 'pramādataḥ apramādo 'vihiṃsā ca jñānayonir asaṃśayam
english: The renunciation of desire when the senses are aroused, vigilance, and non-injury — these are, without doubt, the source of true knowledge.

sanskrit: indriyāṇāṃ yame yatto bhava rājann atandritaḥ buddhiś ca mā te cyavatu niyacchaitāṃ yatas tataḥ
english: Strive diligently, O king, in the restraint of the senses and without sloth; let your intellect not waver — rein it in from wherever it strays.

sanskrit: etaj jñānaṃ vidur viprā dhruvam indriyadhāraṇam etaj jñānaṃ ca panthāś ca yena yānti manīṣiṇaḥ
english: The Brāhmaṇas declare this to be certain knowledge — the steady holding of the senses in check. This is indeed the knowledge and the path by which the wise proceed.

sanskrit: aprāpyaḥ keśavo rājann indriyair ajitair nṛbhiḥ āgamādhigato yogād vaśī tattve prasīdati
english: Keśava cannot be attained, O king, by men whose senses remain unconquered. He who is self-controlled, having approached through scripture and yoga, becomes serene in the truth.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca bhūyo me puṇḍarīkākṣaṃ saṃjayācakṣva pṛcchate nāmakarmārthavit tāta prāpnuyāṃ puruṣottamam
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Tell me further, Sañjaya, of Puṇḍarīkākṣa as I ask — knowing the meaning of his names and deeds, may I attain the Supreme Person.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca śrutaṃ me tasya devasya nāmanirvacanaṃ śubham yāvat tatrābhijāne 'ham aprameyo hi keśavaḥ
english: Sañjaya said: I have heard the auspicious etymological explanation of that god's names, to the extent that I know it — for Keśava is indeed immeasurable.

sanskrit: vasanāt sarvabhūtānāṃ vasutvād devayonitaḥ vāsudevas tato vedyo vṛṣatvād vṛṣṇir ucyate
english: Because he dwells in all beings, because of his divinity as Vasu, and because of his divine origin — he is known as Vāsudeva. Because of his righteousness he is called Vṛṣṇi.

sanskrit: maunād dhyānāc ca yogāc ca viddhi bhārata mādhavam sarvatattvalayāc caiva madhuhā madhusūdanaḥ
english: Know that Mādhava is so called because of his silence, meditation, and yoga, O Bhārata; and Madhusūdana, the slayer of Madhu, is so called because he dissolves into all principles of reality.

sanskrit: kṛṣir bhūvācakaḥ śabdo ṇaś ca nirvṛtivācakaḥ kṛṣṇas tadbhāvayogāc ca kṛṣṇo bhavati śāśvataḥ
english: The syllable 'kri' denotes existence, and 'na' denotes bliss; by the union of these two meanings Kṛṣṇa eternally becomes Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: puṇḍarīkaṃ paraṃ dhāma nityam akṣayam akṣaram tadbhāvāt puṇḍarīkākṣo dasyutrāsāj janārdanaḥ
english: The lotus is the supreme abode, eternal, indestructible, and imperishable; because of that nature he is Puṇḍarīkākṣa. Because he strikes terror into demons he is called Janārdana.

sanskrit: yataḥ sattvaṃ na cyavate yac ca sattvān na hīyate sattvataḥ sātvatas tasmād ārṣabhād vṛṣabhekṣaṇaḥ
english: Because sattva does not depart from him and nothing is diminished from sattva — because of his sattva nature he is called Sātvata, and because of his bull-like excellence he is called Vrishabhekshana.

sanskrit: na jāyate janitryāṃ yad ajas tasmād anīkajit devānāṃ svaprakāśatvād damād dāmodaraṃ viduḥ
english: Because he is not born from a mother he is unborn, and therefore called Anikajit the conqueror of armies. Because he is self-luminous among the gods and because of his self-restraint they know him as Dāmodara.

sanskrit: harṣāt saukhyāt sukhaiśvaryād dhṛṣīkeśatvam aśnute bāhubhyāṃ rodasī bibhran mahābāhur iti smṛtaḥ
english: Because of his joy, happiness, and lordship in bliss he attains the status of Hṛṣīkeśa, lord of the senses. Because with his arms he holds up heaven and earth he is remembered as Mahābāhu, the mighty-armed.

sanskrit: adho na kṣīyate jātu yasmāt tasmād adhokṣajaḥ narāṇām ayanāc cāpi tena nārāyaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ pūraṇāt sadanāc caiva tato 'sau puruṣottamaḥ
english: Because he never diminishes downward he is called Adhokṣaja. Because he is the refuge of men he is remembered as Nārāyaṇa; and because he pervades and is the abode of all, he is the Puruṣottama, the Supreme Person.

sanskrit: asataś ca sataś caiva sarvasya prabhavāpyayāt sarvasya ca sadā jñānāt sarvam enaṃ pracakṣate
english: Because he is the source and dissolution of all that is unreal and real, and because he is ever the knower of all — all things declare him to be everything.

sanskrit: satye pratiṣṭhitaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ satyam atra pratiṣṭhitam satyāt satyaṃ ca govindas tasmāt satyo 'pi nāmataḥ
english: Kṛṣṇa is established in truth, and truth is established in him; Govinda is truth derived from truth — therefore by name he is also called Satya, the True.

sanskrit: viṣṇur vikramaṇād eva jayanāj jiṣṇur ucyate śāśvatatvād anantaś ca govindo vedanād gavām
english: Viṣṇu is so called from his striding; Jiṣṇu from his conquering; Ananta from his eternality; and Govinda from his knowledge of the cows.

sanskrit: atattvaṃ kurute tattvaṃ tena mohayate prajāḥ evaṃvidho dharmanityo bhagavān munibhiḥ saha āgantā hi mahābāhur ānṛśaṃsyārtham acyutaḥ
english: He makes the unreal appear as real and thereby deludes creatures. Such is the nature of the Lord, eternally established in dharma — the mighty-armed Acyuta, the imperishable one, will indeed come together with the sages for the sake of non-cruelty.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca cakṣuṣmatāṃ vai spṛhayāmi saṃjaya; drakṣyanti ye vāsudevaṃ samīpe vibhrājamānaṃ vapuṣā pareṇa; prakāśayantaṃ pradiśo diśaś ca
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: I envy those with sight, O Sañjaya, who will see Vāsudeva nearby, blazing with a transcendent form, illuminating all the quarters and directions.

sanskrit: īrayantaṃ bhāratīṃ bhāratānām; abhyarcanīyāṃ śaṃkarīṃ sṛñjayānām bubhūṣadbhir grahaṇīyām anindyāṃ; parāsūnām agrahaṇīyarūpām
english: — proclaiming speech that is for the Bharatas, worthy of reverence, auspicious for the Sṛñjayas, capable of being grasped by those who desire to know, beyond reproach, and of a form imperceptible to those whose lives are spent.

sanskrit: samudyantaṃ sātvatam ekavīraṃ; praṇetāram ṛṣabhaṃ yādavānām nihantāraṃ kṣobhaṇaṃ śātravāṇāṃ; muṣṇantaṃ ca dviṣatāṃ vai yaśāṃsi
english: — rising as the sole hero of the Sātvata clan, the guide and bull of the Yādavas, the slayer and agitator of enemies, and the one who robs the glory of those who hate him.

sanskrit: draṣṭāro hi kuravas taṃ sametā; mahātmānaṃ śatruhaṇaṃ vareṇyam bruvantaṃ vācam anṛśaṃsarūpāṃ; vṛṣṇiśreṣṭhaṃ mohayantaṃ madīyān
english: For the assembled Kurus will see that great-souled one, the slayer of enemies, the most excellent, speaking words of compassionate form — the best of the Vṛṣṇis — while he bewilders my own people.

sanskrit: ṛṣiṃ sanātanatamaṃ vipaścitaṃ; vācaḥ samudraṃ kalaśaṃ yatīnām ariṣṭanemiṃ garuḍaṃ suparṇaṃ; patiṃ prajānāṃ bhuvanasya dhāma
english: — the most ancient of sages, the wise one, the ocean of speech, the vessel of ascetics, Ariṣṭanemi, Garuḍa, Suparṇa, the lord of creatures, and the abode of the world.

sanskrit: sahasraśīrṣaṃ puruṣaṃ purāṇam; anādimadhyāntam anantakīrtim śukrasya dhātāram ajaṃ janitraṃ; paraṃ parebhyaḥ śaraṇaṃ prapadye
english: I take refuge in the ancient Person of a thousand heads, without beginning, middle, or end, of infinite fame, the supporter of Śukra, the unborn progenitor, the highest refuge beyond all others.

sanskrit: trailokyanirmāṇakaraṃ janitraṃ; devāsurāṇām atha nāgarakṣasām narādhipānāṃ viduṣāṃ pradhānam; indrānujaṃ taṃ śaraṇaṃ prapadye
english: I take refuge in him, the maker and progenitor of the three worlds, the foremost among gods, demons, Nāgas, Rākṣasas, kings, and the learned — the younger brother of Indra.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca saṃjaye pratiyāte tu dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ abhyabhāṣata dāśārham ṛṣabhaṃ sarvasātvatām
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When Sañjaya had departed, King Yudhiṣṭhira the Dharmarāja addressed Janārdana, the bull of the Dāśārha clan, the best of all the Sātvatas.

sanskrit: ayaṃ sa kālaḥ saṃprāpto mitrāṇāṃ me janārdana na ca tvad anyaṃ paśyāmi yo na āpatsu tārayet
english: This is the time, Janārdana, that has come for my friends; and I see no one other than you who can rescue us from calamities.

sanskrit: tvāṃ hi mādhava saṃśritya nirbhayā mohadarpitam dhārtarāṣṭraṃ sahāmātyaṃ svam aṃśam anuyuñjmahe
english: Relying on you, O Mādhava, and free from fear, we seek to reclaim our portion from the Dhārtarāṣṭra who is intoxicated by delusion, together with his ministers.

sanskrit: yathā hi sarvāsv āpatsu pāsi vṛṣṇīn ariṃdama tathā te pāṇḍavā rakṣyāḥ pāhy asmān mahato bhayāt
english: Just as you protect the Vṛṣṇis in all calamities, O conqueror of enemies, so must the Pāṇḍavas be protected by you — protect us from this great danger.

sanskrit: bhagavān uvāca ayam asmi mahābāho brūhi yat te vivakṣitam kariṣyāmi hi tat sarvaṃ yat tvaṃ vakṣyasi bhārata
english: The Lord said: Here I am, O mighty-armed one — speak what you wish to say. I shall do everything that you tell me, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca śrutaṃ te dhṛtarāṣṭrasya saputrasya cikīrṣitam etad dhi sakalaṃ kṛṣṇa saṃjayo māṃ yad abravīt
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: You have heard the intentions of Dhṛtarāṣṭra along with his son — for Sañjaya told me everything in full, O Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: tan mataṃ dhṛtarāṣṭrasya so 'syātmā vivṛtāntaraḥ yathoktaṃ dūta ācaṣṭe vadhyaḥ syād anyathā bruvan
english: That is the mind of Dhṛtarāṣṭra — his inner self stands revealed. A messenger who reports as told must not speak otherwise; to do so would make him liable to death.

sanskrit: apradānena rājyasya śāntim asmāsu mārgati lubdhaḥ pāpena manasā carann asamam ātmanaḥ
english: Without giving back the kingdom, he seeks peace with us — a greedy man, acting with a sinful mind, acting unequally with regard to his own self.

sanskrit: yat tad dvādaśa varṣāṇi vane nirvyuṣitā vayam chadmanā śaradaṃ caikāṃ dhṛtarāṣṭrasya śāsanāt
english: We dwelt in the forest for twelve years and by stealth for one year more — all under the command of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: sthātā naḥ samaye tasmin dhṛtarāṣṭra iti prabho nāhāsma samayaṃ kṛṣṇa tad dhi no brāhmaṇā viduḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra was to abide by that agreement with us, O lord — we did not violate the terms, O Kṛṣṇa; indeed our Brāhmaṇas know this.

sanskrit: vṛddho rājā dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ svadharmaṃ nānupaśyati paśyan vā putragṛddhitvān mandasyānveti śāsanam
english: The old king Dhṛtarāṣṭra does not regard his own duty; or if he sees it, out of greed for his son he follows the command of that foolish one.

sanskrit: suyodhanamate tiṣṭhan rājāsmāsu janārdana mithyā carati lubdhaḥ saṃś caran priyam ivātmanaḥ
english: Standing by the judgment of Suyodhana, the king conducts himself falsely toward us, O Janārdana — a greedy man, acting as though it were pleasing to himself.

sanskrit: ito duḥkhataraṃ kiṃ nu yatrāhaṃ mātaraṃ tataḥ saṃvidhātuṃ na śaknomi mitrāṇāṃ vā janārdana
english: What could be more painful than this — that I cannot provide for my mother, for my father, or for my friends, O Janārdana?

sanskrit: kāśibhiś cedipāñcālair matsyaiś ca madhusūdana bhavatā caiva nāthena pañca grāmā vṛtā mayā
english: With the Kāśi, the Cedi, the Pāñcāla, and the Matsya as allies, and with you as our lord, O Madhusūdana, I have sought only five villages.

sanskrit: kuśasthalaṃ vṛkasthalam āsandī vāraṇāvatam avasānaṃ ca govinda kiṃ cid evātra pañcamam
english: Kushastala, Vrukasthala, Asandi, Vāraṇāvata, and O Govinda, whatever the fifth place among these may be.

sanskrit: pañca nas tāta dīyantāṃ grāmā vā nagarāṇi vā vasema sahitā yeṣu mā ca no bharatā naśan
english: Let five be given to us, my dear — whether villages or towns — in which we may dwell together, so that the Bharatas may not perish.

sanskrit: na ca tān api duṣṭātmā dhārtarāṣṭro 'numanyate svāmyam ātmani matvāsāv ato duḥkhataraṃ nu kim
english: Yet even those the wicked-souled Dhārtarāṣṭra will not consent to, considering himself the sole lord. What could be more painful than this?

sanskrit: kule jātasya vṛddhasya paravitteṣu gṛdhyataḥ lobhaḥ prajñānam āhanti prajñā hanti hatā hriyam
english: In one well-born, grown old, yet covetous of another's wealth — greed destroys wisdom; and wisdom, once destroyed, slays shame.

sanskrit: hrīr hatā bādhate dharmaṃ dharmo hanti hataḥ śriyam śrīr hatā puruṣaṃ hanti puruṣasyāsvatā vadhaḥ
english: Shame, once slain, oppresses dharma; dharma, once slain, destroys prosperity; prosperity, once destroyed, slays the man; and the destruction of a man is his destitution.

sanskrit: asvato hi nivartante jñātayaḥ suhṛdartvijaḥ apuṣpād aphalād vṛkṣād yathā tāta patatriṇaḥ
english: From the destitute man, kinsmen, friends, and priests depart, O dear one — as birds depart from a tree that has neither flowers nor fruit.

sanskrit: etac ca maraṇaṃ tāta yad asmāt patitād iva jñātayo vinivartante pretasattvād ivāsavaḥ
english: This indeed is death, O dear one — that kinsmen turn away from one who has fallen, as the vital breaths withdraw from a dying being.

sanskrit: nātaḥ pāpīyasīṃ kāṃ cid avasthāṃ śambaro 'bravīt yatra naivādya na prātar bhojanaṃ pratidṛśyate
english: Śambara declared that there is no more wretched condition than this — where no food is seen either today or tomorrow.

sanskrit: dhanam āhuḥ paraṃ dharmaṃ dhane sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam jīvanti dhanino loke mṛtā ye tv adhanā narāḥ
english: They say that wealth is the highest dharma; in wealth all things are established. The wealthy live in the world; those men without wealth are as good as dead.

sanskrit: ye dhanād apakarṣanti naraṃ svabalam āśritāḥ te dharmam arthaṃ kāmaṃ ca pramathnanti naraṃ ca tam
english: Those who, relying on their own strength, strip a man of his wealth — they crush dharma, artha, and kama, and that man himself.

sanskrit: etām avasthāṃ prāpyaike maraṇaṃ vavrire janāḥ grāmāyaike vanāyaike nāśāyaike pravavrajuḥ
english: Reaching this condition, some men have chosen death; some have gone to the village, some to the forest, and some have taken to wandering in despair.

sanskrit: unmādam eke puṣyanti yānty anye dviṣatāṃ vaśam dāsyam eke nigacchanti pareṣām arthahetunā
english: Some cultivate madness; others fall under the sway of enemies; some fall into servitude to others for the sake of wealth.

sanskrit: āpad evāsya maraṇāt puruṣasya garīyasī śriyo vināśas tad dhy asya nimittaṃ dharmakāmayoḥ
english: Calamity is heavier for a man than death itself — the destruction of prosperity is indeed the cause of the ruin of both dharma and desire for him.

sanskrit: yad asya dharmyaṃ maraṇaṃ śāśvataṃ lokavartma tat samantāt sarvabhūtānāṃ na tad atyeti kaś cana
english: For that death which is his righteous end, that eternal way of the world — no being whatsoever escapes it on all sides.

sanskrit: na tathā bādhyate kṛṣṇa prakṛtyā nirdhano janaḥ yathā bhadrāṃ śriyaṃ prāpya tayā hīnaḥ sukhaidhitaḥ
english: A man who is poor by nature is not afflicted so greatly, O Kṛṣṇa, as one who has obtained good fortune and then, having been nourished in ease, is deprived of it.

sanskrit: sa tadātmāparādhena saṃprāpto vyasanaṃ mahat sendrān garhayate devān nātmānaṃ ca kathaṃ cana
english: He, having reached great misfortune through his own fault, blames the gods along with Indra — but never blames himself in any way.

sanskrit: na cāsmin sarvaśāstrāṇi prataranti nigarhaṇām so 'bhikrudhyati bhṛtyānāṃ suhṛdaś cābhyasūyati
english: And no amount of scripture can restrain him from blame; he grows angry at his servants and becomes envious of his friends.

sanskrit: taṃ tadā manyur evaiti sa bhūyaḥ saṃpramuhyati sa mohavaśam āpannaḥ krūraṃ karma niṣevate
english: Wrath then overtakes him; he becomes further deluded; and having fallen under the power of delusion, he pursues cruel deeds.

sanskrit: pāpakarmātyayāyaiva saṃkaraṃ tena puṣyati saṃkaro narakāyaiva sā kāṣṭhā pāpakarmaṇām
english: Through excess of sinful deeds he nurtures confusion; confusion leads only to hell — that is the final destination of sinful deeds.

sanskrit: na cet prabudhyate kṛṣṇa narakāyaiva gacchati tasya prabodhaḥ prajñaiva prajñācakṣur na riṣyati
english: If he does not awaken, O Kṛṣṇa, he goes only to hell; his awakening is wisdom itself, and the eye of wisdom is never destroyed.

sanskrit: prajñālābhe hi puruṣaḥ śāstrāṇy evānvavekṣate śāstranityaḥ punar dharmaṃ tasya hrīr aṅgam uttamam
english: When a man gains wisdom he then studies the scriptures; and one ever devoted to scripture regains dharma — the highest limb of which is shame.

sanskrit: hrīmān hi pāpaṃ pradveṣṭi tasya śrīr abhivardhate śrīmān sa yāvad bhavati tāvad bhavati pūruṣaḥ
english: The man endowed with shame hates sin; his prosperity grows; and as long as that man prospers, so long does he truly be a man.

sanskrit: dharmanityaḥ praśāntātmā kāryayogavahaḥ sadā nādharme kurute buddhiṃ na ca pāpeṣu vartate
english: Ever devoted to dharma, calm in soul, ever diligent in the performance of duty — he does not turn his mind to adharma and does not dwell in sinful acts.

sanskrit: ahrīko vā vimūḍho vā naiva strī na punaḥ pumān nāsyādhikāro dharme 'sti yathā śūdras tathaiva saḥ
english: One who is without shame, or who is thoroughly deluded — such a one is neither woman nor man; he has no claim to dharma, just as a Śūdra has none.

sanskrit: hrīmān avati devāṃś ca pitṝn ātmānam eva ca tenāmṛtatvaṃ vrajati sā kāṣṭhā puṇyakarmaṇām
english: The person endowed with shame protects the gods, the ancestors, and himself as well; through that he attains immortality — that is the final destination of virtuous deeds.

sanskrit: tad idaṃ mayi te dṛṣṭaṃ pratyakṣaṃ madhusūdana yathā rājyāt paribhraṣṭo vasāmi vasatīr imāḥ
english: All this you can see directly in my case, O Madhusūdana — how, fallen from my kingdom, I dwell in these lodgings.

sanskrit: te vayaṃ na śriyaṃ hātum alaṃ nyāyena kena cit atra no yatamānānāṃ vadhaś ced api sādhu tat
english: We cannot rightly abandon prosperity under any argument; and if death comes upon us while we strive for it, even that would be good.

sanskrit: tatra naḥ prathamaḥ kalpo yad vayaṃ te ca mādhava praśāntāḥ samabhūtāś ca śriyaṃ tān aśnuvīmahi
english: The first option for us would be, O Mādhava, that we and they become peaceful and equal in spirit, and that we together enjoy that prosperity.

sanskrit: tatraiṣā paramā kāṣṭhā raudrakarmakṣayodayā yad vayaṃ kauravān hatvā tāni rāṣṭrāṇy aśīmahi
english: The ultimate extreme — born from the destruction of terrible deeds — would be that we slay the Kauravas and then enjoy those kingdoms.

sanskrit: ye punaḥ syur asaṃbaddhā anāryāḥ kṛṣṇa śatravaḥ teṣām apy avadhaḥ kāryaḥ kiṃ punar ye syur īdṛśāḥ
english: Even enemies who are unrelated and ignoble must be slain — how much more so those who are of this kind?

sanskrit: jñātayaś ca hi bhūyiṣṭhāḥ sahāyā guravaś ca naḥ teṣāṃ vadho 'tipāpīyān kiṃ nu yuddhe 'sti śobhanam
english: For our allies are mostly kinsmen and elders — the slaying of them is exceedingly sinful. What then is glorious in battle?

sanskrit: pāpaḥ kṣatriyadharmo 'yaṃ vayaṃ ca kṣatrabāndhavāḥ sa naḥ svadharmo 'dharmo vā vṛttir anyā vigarhitā
english: This dharma of the Kṣatriya is sinful, and we are bound by kinship to Kṣatriyas — it is our own prescribed duty, whether dharma or adharma, since any other livelihood is condemned.
